title: kind:26006 — hold alarm
description:
The live nudge, and the ONLY live path to a hold. The fork makes 46010 channel-scoped, and fan_out_scoped routes a channel-bearing event through the channel indexes only while a REQ with no #h registers globally — the invariant is stated outright in the source at crates/buzz-relay/src/subscription.rs:487-492. A REQ of {kinds:[46010],"#p":[me]} therefore cannot deliver a hold and no document may specify one.

NEVER COALESCED, NEVER SHED. The <=400 ms end-to-end budget is on this frame, not on the durable row.

A NUDGE WITH NO AUTHORITY. It triggers the needs-action query; a row appears only if the daemon-backed hold list confirms it. A Perch that is disconnected when the alarm fires MISSES IT — ephemerals are never stored — so the query also runs on connect and on every reconnect.

GLOBAL, NO h TAG, AND `26006` IS ADDED TO P_GATED_KINDS. This is the ratified answer to the alarm-disclosure hole; it is ADR 0017 clause C3 and APPENDIX-NORMATIVE.md section 3's 'global (no h)' survives unchanged. 13-WIRE-SCHEMAS.md amendment W-1 previously specified an h tag naming a standing #watch channel; W-1 is WITHDRAWN and W-9 records why in one sentence: the p-gate does not run on a channel-scoped subscription. crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/req.rs:218 wraps p_gated_filters_authorized in `if channel_id.is_none()`, with the comment at :215-217 saying so — 'Only applies to GLOBAL subscriptions (channel_id = None)'. So an h-tagged 26006 is delivered through the channel index, where the gate is never consulted, and any member of the #watch channel opening {kinds:[26006],"#h":[watch]} would receive every operator's alarms. The h tag narrows the disclosure ring; it does not close it. It also silently breaks the only shipped client filter (skeleton/desktop/src/shared/api/perchSubscriptions.ts writes a global {kinds:[26006],"#p":[me],limit:0}), which would deliver zero frames with nothing failing loudly.

WHAT C3 BUYS. With 26006 in P_GATED_KINDS (crates/buzz-core/src/kind.rs:159-169, which already carries KIND_AGENT_OBSERVER_FRAME — an ephemeral, included for exactly this filter-layer enforcement, per the doc comment at :156-158), p_gated_filters_authorized (req.rs:1182-1215) requires every global filter naming 26006 to carry a #p whose values are ALL the authed pubkey (:1211-1213) and CLOSEs the subscription otherwise with 'restricted: p-gated events require #p matching your pubkey'. A member cannot subscribe to another operator's alarms at all. The cost is one line in buzz-core — a THIRD fork site beyond the two ingest.rs arms — which is brief amendment AD-A7's framing: 'three hunks in buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs and one line in buzz-core/src/kind.rs; zero client registration points'.

issuer.description: The bridge's spine identity, for display only. THE ADMITTED-ISSUER RULE MATCHES THE NOSTR EVENT'S `pubkey`, NOT THIS FIELD — this one is inside the content an adversary controls.

seq.description: Per-kind monotonic counter assigned by the bridge. A gap between two frames the console actually received proves loss on a live connection; it says nothing about frames emitted while the console was disconnected, because ephemerals are never stored (crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/event.rs:794-906 writes nothing to Postgres in either branch).

hold_id.description: Opaque random token. Never derived from hunt_id — this frame is the widest-audience object in the registry and hunt_id is a join key into detection data.

x-transport.why_no_relay_change_for_the_EPHEMERAL_PA: handle_event short-circuits every 20000-29999 kind into handle_ephemeral_event and RETURNS at crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/event.rs:751, before ingest_event is reached at :761, so required_scope_for_kind never sees a 26xxx. Proved in-tree by the test ephemeral_kinds_not_in_scope_allowlist at crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs:3851-3854. The INGEST path needs no change; the READ path needs the one P_GATED_KINDS line below.
x-transport.websocket_only: POST /events goes straight into ingest_event (crates/buzz-relay/src/api/bridge.rs:925) with no ephemeral branch, so an HTTP-posted 26xxx is rejected 'restricted: unknown event kind'. The bridge must hold a live WebSocket.
x-transport.h_tag: NONE. Channel-less, published through the Uuid::nil() global routing sentinel at crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/event.rs:875-903.
x-transport.p_tags: one per Approve-scoped operator principal. Under P_GATED_KINDS these stop being a client-side paging hint and become the relay's own authorization test.
x-transport.relay_change_required: ONE LINE: add KIND_RESPONSE_HELD_ALARM (26006) to P_GATED_KINDS in crates/buzz-core/src/kind.rs:159-169. Owned by adr/0017 clause C3 and 10-RELAY-FORK.md; the two-connection E2E that proves a non-p-tagged member is CLOSEd belongs with it.
